title: Sforno on Leviticus
text: אדם כי יקריב מכם, when he brings from himself close to G’d with confession of his sins and submission in the way of the verse in Hoseah 14,3 ונשלמה פרים שפתינו, “So we will offer the words of our lips instead of bulls.” And as it says in Psalms 51,19  זבחי אלוקים רוח נשברה, “The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit.” For he has no desire for fools who bring offerings without a (sense) of prior submission (to God), and our Sages have already said, “מכם,” from you, and not all of you, to exclude the Mumar (apostate).

At this point the Torah warns that one must not cause distress to one’s fellow man by undermining his dignity, his self image and the image he enjoys among his peers. Example are: לא תקלל חרש, this is a damage that the deaf person does not even become aware of. Next, the Torah discusses tangible damages, such as

לפני עור לא תתן מכשול, indirect damages, for who knows if the blind will trip over the obstacle? The one causing even indirect damage is held responsible by the Torah. [this is presumably in the realm of heavenly judgment, seeing that the Talmud feels that people, as opposed to animals, who have eyes in their head, should watch out for obstacles in their path. Ed.]

(1) ADONAI SAID TO MOSHE, SAY TO THE PRIESTS.  What was said above -- to understand and to instruct regarding all sorts of impurities, to distinguish between the pure and impure domestic beasts and between the pure and impure birds, for this is more appropriate for the priests, according to what He said, "to distinguish between the holy and the profane, and between the pure and  the impure."

(2) AND SAY TO THEM.  That they must refrain not only from these, but also from the impurity of a corpse and from profaning their seed, for these are qualities of holiness applicable to the priests alone.  ...

(3) HE SHALL NOT BECOME IMPURE FOR A [DEAD] PERSON AMONG HIS KIN.  No one among the priests shall become impure for a [dead] person among "his people" -- i.e., any dead person among the multitudes who is not among his relatives, but is simply "from his people."

A CHIEF SHALL NOT BECOME IMPURE FOR ONE AMONG HIS PEOPLE [JPS:  BUT HE SHALL NOT DEFILE HIMSELF AS A KINSMAN BY MARRIAGE] AND SO PROFANE HIMSELF.  And the reason why the priest must not become impure except for his relatives is that the priest is in fact "a chief among his people" to understand and to instruct, "for the lips of a priest guard knowledge, And rulings are sought from his mouth" (Mal. 2:7).  And it is appropriate for a person like this to comport himself like a prince "so that his words will be heeded," and it is not appropriate to profane his eligibility for the Sanctuary and its appurtenances to honor dead persons who are not his relatives, as they said (Sanh. 47a), that the burial and the eulogy for the dead person are "honor to the deceased" [as opposed to being honor to the mourners].  However, for relatives, [the Torah] permits becoming impure, for the honor to them is an honor to him.

THEY SHALL NOT SHAVE.  Even though I have allowed them impurity for their dead for their own honor, I have not allowed them to be extreme in their mourning to increase the honor to their dead by shaving and scarifying, as they, z"l, said (Sifra, ch. 1:3), "just as there it is over the dead, so here it is over the dead."

THEY SHALL NOT PROFANE THE NAME OF THEIR GOD.  Even though all of these are for the sake of his honor, he is not entitled to forgo his honor, for in fact the point of the honor of the priests is for the honor of God, may He be blessed, and when they forgo this, they desecrate His name.

FOR HE IS HOLY TO HIS [JPS: THEY ARE HOLY TO THEIR] GOD.  Each descendant of the priesthood, being a chief among his people, is holy to his God, and if he marries these women, he will profane his honor and his seed, who will not be fit for that holiness.

ADONAI SPOKE TO MOSHE ON MT. SINAI.  Now [the Torah] does not mention the location of the command in the case of any mitzva unless something new happened in that place, but [here] it clarifies that when God, may He be exalted, said on Sinai (Ex. 23:11), "in the seventh you shall let it rest and lie fallow. Let the needy among your people eat of it, etc..," He then explained to Moshe all the laws the laws of the seventh year that are stated in this place, to understand and to instruct.  And this itself was [the case] for all other mitzvot, for even though, in some of their cases, what was said was only brief Scripture, the clarification then was expansive, with great clarity.  As they, z"l, said, "What is the relevance of Sh'mita to Mr.Sinai? But just as, in the case of Sh'mita, its general rules, explanations, and details were spoken on Sinai, so all the other mitzvot -- their general rules, explanations, and details were spoken on Sinai.  And Moshe our Teacher mentions this section in this place because he thought that they would immediately be entering the land, as he testified when he said (Num. 10:29), "we are setting out for the place."  And he enjoined them regarding the sh'mita of the soil in particular because it was from their sin regarding its observance that they would be exiled from it, as it testifies in saying (Lev. 26:34), "Then shall the land make up for its sabbath years," and it testifies similarly at the end of Chronicles, in saying (II Chron. 26:21), "until the land paid back its sabbaths."
(1) WHEN YOU ENTER THE LAND.  The "Galilee of the Nations" (Isa. 8:23).
(2) THE LAND SHALL REST.  The soil that is ready for the work of the land.

(3) A SABBATH OF ADONAI.  That the whole year that is idle from working the land will be ready for service to Him, as He intended regarding Shabbat, as He said (Exod. 20:10), "a Shabbat of Adonai your God."

(1) SIX YEARS YOU CAN [JPS: MAY] SOW YOUR FIELD.  Then you will be able to sow a single field, through its strength, six years in a row, which is contrary to the principles of farming, for in fact the custom regarding it is that it should be fallow one year and he should sow it one year, as our Rabbis mentioned.
(2) YOU WILL GATHER ITS YIELD.  Contrary to the custom in farming, that, if they sow its portion in its strength for consecutive years, it will not continue to yield its strength.

(1) THE LAND SHALL HAVE A SABBATH OF COMPLETE REST.  Even from merely preparatory farmwork, like placing manure on [cut] trees, smearing oil [on pruned trees], perforating unripe fruit, and the sort, that they, z"l, mentioned.  ...
(2) A SABBATH OF ADONAI.  Also the farm workers, when they rest that year, will be aroused to seek Adonai in some way.
